findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket, so objects are stored unencrypted by default rather than encryption being the default state for stored data.

findings.issue_category: missing access control / public access block
findings.description: No ACL or public access block configuration is set, leaving the bucket potentially subject to default/broader access; no bucket policy or aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource restricts public access.
The bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so sensitive ledger export data is stored without encryption at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is specified, so model artifacts are stored unencrypted despite versioning and logging being configured.
The bucket lacks a server_side_encryption_configuration block, leaving operational runbook data unencrypted at rest.

The acl value 'lcatalogopts-delivery-write' is not a valid S3 canned ACL (the intended value was likely 'log-delivery-write'); this typo could cause deployment failure or unintended default access behavior, undermining the intended restrictive access control for the audit log bucket.
force_destroy = true allows the bucket and all its contents to be deleted without recovery, increasing risk of accidental or malicious data loss for archived reports.
force_destroy = true permits deletion of the bucket and all ledger export objects without a safeguard, risking loss of financial data.

findings.issue_category: destructive operation enabled on audit logs
findings.description: force_destroy = true on the audit trail bucket allows deletion of audit logs, undermining the integrity and availability of the security audit trail.

The uploaded object does not specify server-side encryption (e.g., kms_key_id or server_side_encryption) and is placed in a bucket with no default encryption, so the vendor roster file is stored in plaintext.
